answer: Cross-Epoch Identity Ridge. Each identity accumulates a per-epoch behavioural signal vector from its task mix, timing, and interaction graph; the agent must stay within a learned ridge around its own prior trajectory, and a clone spun up fresh cannot fabricate that history without replaying it. Enforcement compares current-epoch vectors to the identity's own past, not to peers, so copying another agent's pigment of behaviour fails the self-consistency test.
